messages:
Marta: Heads-up — proposing a focused game-day: forced preemptions on mixed-capacity GPU pools this Wed 09:00 PT. Goal: validate eviction handling, fallback routing, and SLOs for short-lived jobs. 

Raj: +1. Can we scope to two regions (us-west2, eu-central1) and include one Dedicated pool + two spot pools with different bid strategies?

Marta: Yes. Plan: 
- us-west2: dedicated + spot-A (aggressive, cheaper) + spot-B (balanced)
- eu-central1: dedicated + spot-A only
- Run small and medium workloads (inferencing and batch preprocessing)

Chris: What counts as success? Need measurable criteria.

Marta: Proposed success criteria: 
1) No customer-facing 5xx increase beyond baseline +200% for >5m (ops alert).
2) 95th pct tail latency for single-request inference stays <1500ms in hosted routes (canary).
3) Automatic fallback to compatible model variant or region completes <30s for routed requests.
4) KV cache hit-rate degradation <10% vs baseline.
5) No tokenized data leaked to logs (audit).

Olivia: For fallback: are we using region failover or model-variant downgrade? Need to spell order.

Raj: Routing policy = prefer dedicated -> spot-B -> spot-A. On eviction, immediate reroute to next available pool. If same region capacity exhausted, route to remote region with throttle.

Devon: I'll instrument a synthetic workload harness. Will run steady 120 qps (small ctx) + occasional burst of 600 qps for 60s.

Chris: How are we forcing preemptions? Provider-sim or in-cluster eviction? Prefer using cloud provider API to terminate spot instances to mirror real behavior. Also a lower-level test: we can kill processes on VMs to exercise node-level failure.

Marta: Do both. Provider API for nominal evictions; process kills for K8s pod eviction paths. Sequence: 1) baseline 15m 2) provider evictions (10-30% of spot nodes over 5m) 3) process kills 4) scale-backs (simulate capacity pressure) 5) recovery window.

InfraBot: new run created: <https://ci.redwood.ai/gamedays/1779994321-run|gameday-1779994321>. Test matrix: 2 regions, 3 pool types, 3 workload profiles. Logs will stream to /logs/gamedays/1779994321.

Olivia: Prometheus alerts to watch (suggested):
```
ALERT High5xxRate
  IF sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route) > 2 * baseline
  FOR 5m
```
```
ALERT FallbackFail
  IF increase(fallback_errors_total[5m]) > 0
```

Raj: Also add a dashboard panel for per-pool token cost and per-token latency breakdown (infer/encoder/kvcache). We need to see the cost delta for spot evictions.

Devon: I'll add a small harness that records per-request routing path (pool ids), fallback events, and token consumption. Output format will be newline-delimited JSON to GCS.

Chris: Important: ensure checkpointed KV caches survive across fallback where possible. If we reroute to model-variant w/out shared cache, we'll see major latency spikes. Add a test case that forces cache miss to measure degradation.

Marta: Ops playbook excerpt we will follow during the drill: 
- T+0: Start baseline (notify #general and #oncall)
- T+15m: Start provider-side evictions (API kills)
- T+22m: Trigger process-level kills on 30% of nodes in spot-A
- T+30m: Sudden scale-down in eu-central1 spot-B to simulate regional capacity crunch
- T+40m: Run recovery (bring back instances, revert routing)
- Post-mortem: collect metrics and logs, run evals on quality regression set

Devon: Can someone post the exact kubectl drain command we should use for graceful evictions in the process-kill phase?

Raj: Use: 
```
kubectl cordon <node-name>
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Note: for GPU pods with local scratch, force is needed in some cases.

Olivia: Also include the eviction-sim script snippet (cloud API call):
```
# GCP preemptible simulate: delete instances by name from instance group
gcloud compute instances delete INSTANCE_NAME --zone=ZONE --quiet
```

Chris: For observability: log correlation is essential. Correlate request-id -> token-cost -> pool-id. Add trace attributes: pool_id, node_id, eviction_reason, fallback_target.

Marta: Runbook escalation: if 5xx spike lasts >10m escalate to SRE lead and pause synthetic workload. If tail latency > 2x SLO for >15m cut traffic to dedicated fallback route.

Devon: I'm worried about billing surprises. If fallback routes to remote region with on-demand reserved, cost could spike. Add a hard budget throttle in the harness to stop synthetic load at cost $X/hour.

Raj: Good call. We should simulate cost alarm that triggers traffic shaping. I'll add a policy: if per-minute projected cost > threshold, reduce consumer QPS by 50% via token bucket.

InfraBot: Reminder: attach perm ACLs for access to logs: game-day-readers group. Also auto-archive workspace after 7d.

Olivia: Any security concerns? We'll ensure test data is synthetic and flagged. No keys or PII in logs.

Chris: One more: check autoscaler behavior for GPUs. In past tests the cluster-autoscaler took 90-120s to provision new nodes. That will affect our 30s fallback target — we need model-variant downgrade as primary fallback and region fallback as secondary.

Marta: Updated routing order: 1) dedicated (same region) 2) compatible quantized model-variant (same region) 3) spot-B 4) spot-A 5) remote dedicated. Quantized model-variant should be able to accept prefix-KV or warm start within 20s.

Devon: I'll schedule the run and attach the harness config. Also adding an automatic smoke test after recovery which runs 200 end-to-end prompts and compares answers to baseline (quality regression check).

Raj: Post-game tasks: (a) update fallback docs with measured timings (b) tune autoscaler provisioning buffer (c) add model-variant warmers to reduce cold-starts.

Marta: Thanks team. Final checklist before Wed: confirm ACLs, infra run link (InfraBot), canary keys, and notify customer-success for any tenant tone-down. Anyone picking run lead?

Chris: I'll be run lead. Olivia on observability, Devon on harness, Raj on routing config. Marta will coordinate post-mortem.

Marta: Perfect. I'll post the formal invite and add the checklist to the run page. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: run 1779994321 status: scheduled for 2026-04-01T16:00:00Z. Participants: Marta, Chris, Olivia, Raj, Devon. Logs will appear under /logs/gamedays/1779994321.
